note: 16 targets. Roster is deep (1-0, strong starting core), so this board skews WATCH/AVOID -- three moves clear the bar for an actual roster swap this week: Wentz for real QB2 insurance (I rostered zero backup behind Mahomes), Gesicki over Ferguson at TE2, and Hollins over Johnston at bench WR. Several Jaguars/Cowboys backfield names are pure handcuffs on my own rostered starters (Tuten, Javonte Williams).

targets.hook: Fills empty QB2 slot -- I own zero backup behind Mahomes
targets.why: Mahomes is my only rostered QB in a shallow-QB format, a real structural gap even before this week's Sleeper snapshot showed my QB slot unset. Wentz relieved Kyler Murray (concussion protocol) in Week 1, throwing for 133 yards and 3 touchdowns, and is expected to start Week 2 at Chicago if Murray doesn't clear in time (Star Tribune, 2026-09-14) -- a real streaming floor while he doubles as my only QB2 insurance.
targets.asset: 13/19, 133 yds, 3 TD in relief, Week 1; confirmed Week 2 starter pending Murray's protocol status
targets.rate_basis: recent-trend (wk 1 relief appearance, likely wk 2 start)
targets.my_team_impact: I only own Mahomes at QB. Wentz is cheap insurance against a Mahomes bye (week 10) or injury, and a real streamer in his own right while Murray is out.
targets.confidence_why: The Week 2 starting role is well-sourced; the value is purely as backup insurance, not a lineup upgrade, which caps how much it's worth spending.
targets.competition: No rival in this league is short at QB right now, so this clears cheap.
targets.bid: 2 dollars, a routine-uncontested price for pure QB2 insurance, not a starter
targets.drop: Kayshon Boutte is buried in a crowded Houston WR room behind Collins and Boutte's own teammates; scoopable if dropped.

targets.hook: Bengals' clear TE1/slot weapon: 7 targets, 78 yds, TD Wk1
targets.why: Gesicki led Cincinnati in catches, targets and receiving yards in Week 1 (5/7 for 78 yards and a TD), working as a de facto slot receiver behind Chase and Higgins commanding coverage attention. TE is this league's shallowest skill position by design (only 10 startable TE slots, no dedicated TE-premium scoring), so a clear No.-1-target tight end on the wire is a real market inefficiency, not just a name (CBS Sports, 2026-09-14).
targets.asset: 5 rec / 7 tgt / 78 yds / 1 TD in Week 1, TE4 in points scored through Sunday
targets.rate_basis: recent-trend (wk 1, first data point of the season)
targets.my_team_impact: My TE2 is Jake Ferguson, a middling Dallas option. Gesicki's clean No.-1-target TE role is a direct upgrade in bye-week/injury insurance and gives me a real TE2 with standalone flex value if LaPorta misses time, rather than a name I never actually start.
targets.confidence_why: One-game sample, but the role (leading the team in every receiving category with Chase/Higgins drawing coverage) is structural, not a fluke stat line.
targets.competition: Sladsous and DadKing each carry only one rostered TE (Kincaid, Likely) and could speculate on a TE2; neither has a large-sample FAAB history to price off, so this stays inside the routine band.
targets.bid: 6 dollars, clears a light speculative bid from a single-TE roster without overpaying for a Week 1 sample
targets.drop: Jake Ferguson is the same TE2 tier without Gesicki's clear target funnel; not scoopable, a low-appetite Dallas TE.
